saints.name: St. John of the Cross
saints.title: Priest and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: A Carmelite reformer and poet of the mystical life, who sang of the dark night of the soul and its union with God…
biography: Juan de Yepes was born in 1542 at Fontiveros, near Ávila, and grew up in poverty after his father's early death. He entered the Carmelites at Medina del Campo in 1563, studied at Salamanca, and was ordained priest in 1567. That same year he met Teresa of Ávila, who won him to her reform; in 1568 he established the first house of Discalced friars at Duruelo, taking the name John of the Cross.

The unreformed friars seized him in 1577 and held him nine months in a narrow cell at Toledo, where he composed the first stanzas of the Spiritual Canticle; escaping in 1578, he continued the reform in Andalusia. His treatises — the Ascent of Mount Carmel, the Dark Night, the Spiritual Canticle, the Living Flame of Love — chart the soul's way through purification to union with God and are classics both of theology and of Spanish verse.

He died at Úbeda on 14 December 1591, was canonized by Benedict XIII in 1726, and was declared a Doctor of the Church by Pius XI in 1926. The poet of the dark night is the patron of mystics, of contemplatives, and of Spanish poets.
saints.knownFor: His mystical poetry and the reform of Carmel.
